rule: Existing sourceQuality and sourceUrl are claims from the current corpus; they are NOT certification of text or live link destination. Every prayer/novena is pending comparison against its original witness before ACCEPTED.

conflicts.source: Holy See Compendium French Appendix A, Acte d’espérance
conflicts.note: The official French printed source says « Dans cette foi » while Latin says « In hac spe » and English says « In this hope ». Preserve source wording, do not silently emend.
Separate the Litanies from the following psalm/collect and collate EN/FR; segment ownership addressed in PR #711 but texts not certified.
Keep post-Seventh Word Marian prayers as appendix rather than seventh meditation.

collation.summary: The three common-prayer formulas are present in the printed 2005 Compendium; punctuation and capitalization do not constitute independent source certifications.

French app text uses the older vous / ne nous laissez pas succomber formula; the 2005 French Compendium instead uses tu / ne nous soumets pas. An early nineteenth-century French catechism witnesses the traditional construction, but its surrounding wording is not an exact line-for-line match.

relatedWitnesses.label: Traditional French catechism (historical comparison, not exact app edition)

uiNotice.en: The French text is the traditional form; it is not the wording of the linked French 2005 Compendium.
uiNotice.fr: La version française conserve la formule traditionnelle ; elle n’est pas identique au texte français du Compendium de 2005.

collation.summary: Common Hail Mary formula appears in EN/FR/Latin published appendix; minor punctuation and typographical differences require normalized text comparison.
Common Gloria Patri appears in EN/FR/Latin published appendix; minor spelling and punctuation differences.

App French says je crois au Saint-Esprit, while the 2005 French Compendium says je crois en l'Esprit Saint. Traditional French catechetical use of Saint-Esprit is historically attested; preserve wording and distinguish the French source edition.

uiNotice.en: The app's French Creed preserves the traditional Saint-Esprit and Ainsi soit-il. The 2005 French Compendium instead prints Esprit Saint and ends Amen. The two French witnesses should be compared, not treated as verbatim twins.
uiNotice.fr: Le Credo de l’application conserve « Saint-Esprit » et « Ainsi soit-il ». Le Compendium français de 2005 emploie « Esprit Saint » dans la profession et termine par « Amen ». Ce sont deux témoins distincts.

collation.summary: The 2005 English and Latin Acts of Contrition have an extended punishment/occasion structure. The French printed Acte de contrition is appreciably shorter. They are distinct official local forms, not three literal translations of one text.

uiNotice.en: The Compendium's French Act of Contrition is shorter than its English and Latin prayers and does not print the final « Amen » shown here. The app retains that customary ending without claiming a verbatim copy.
uiNotice.fr: L’Acte de contrition français du Compendium est plus court que les formes anglaise et latine et n’imprime pas l’« Amen » final présent ici. Cette conclusion usuelle est conservée sans prétendre copier l’édition mot à mot.

collation.summary: The printed Compendium's English Act of Faith includes an expanded Trinitarian/Christological section absent from its concise Latin and French forms. All are attested there; do not imply word-for-word translation.

uiNotice.en: The English Act of Faith in the 2005 Compendium includes longer Trinitarian and Christological clauses than its French and Latin forms. They are separately published prayers, not three literal translations.
uiNotice.fr: L’Acte de foi anglais du Compendium de 2005 comporte des développements trinitaire et christologique absents des formules française et latine. Ce ne sont pas trois traductions mot à mot.

collation.summary: The Holy See's printed French Acte d'espérance ends Dans cette foi while English ends In this hope and Latin In hac spe. Preserve the attested French reading until an independently witnessed correction is found; previous UI disclosure remains canonical.
French published Acte de charité omits the English/Latin closing In this love I intend to live and die, and is shorter; the app follows these distinct official formulas.

uiNotice.en: The French published Act of Charity ends sooner than the English and Latin forms, which include a final resolution to live and die in charity. The app preserves the separate published language forms.
uiNotice.fr: L’Acte de charité français publié se termine avant les formules anglaise et latine, qui ajoutent une résolution de vivre et mourir dans la charité. Chaque version est conservée selon son témoin.

collation.summary: The English verse, French Ange de Dieu and Latin Angele Dei appear in the respective Compendium appendices and match the app substantially.

The original historical Baltimore Manual Morning Prayers page contains Grace Before Meals. App English substantially reproduces the prayer, including the shorter conclusion; French still lacks a fully independently collated printed witness.

The cited Baltimore Manual has We give Thee thanks ... for all Thy mercies, while the app says ... for all Thy benefits, a documented alternative preserved in Blessed Sacrament Book / Prayers During the Day. The extra responsories in historical books must not be silently ascribed to the app.

relatedWitnesses.label: Blessed Sacrament Book, prayers during the day

uiNotice.en: The Blessed Sacrament Book prints benefits, matching the app's opening. Its printed sequence then includes Vouchsafe and Let us bless before the prayer for faithful departed; the app deliberately omits those intervening sections and is a shortened composite, not an uninterrupted facsimile. The Baltimore Manual uses mercies.
uiNotice.fr: Le Blessed Sacrament Book donne « benefits », comme le début de la prière. Le livre intercale ensuite Vouchsafe et Let us bless avant la prière pour les défunts ; l’application omet ces passages. C’est un assemblage abrégé, non la transcription continue de la page. Le manuel de Baltimore emploie « mercies ».

collation.summary: App French Salve Regina uses vous, Reine and an older conventional vocabulary, whereas the French 2005 Compendium uses Salut, ô Reine and tutoiement. Latin and English belong to the corresponding common prayer; no exact French 2005-text identity.

relatedWitnesses.label: French Marian text, historical-style comparison (not exact edition)

uiNotice.en: The French Salve Regina is a traditional translation, not the exact wording of the French 2005 Compendium. This prayer also appends Pray for us and its response; the printed Compendium reference contains only the antiphon, so the appended verses must be verified separately.
uiNotice.fr: Le Salve Regina français est une traduction traditionnelle, distincte du Compendium français de 2005. La prière ajoute aussi « Priez pour nous » et sa réponse, absents de l’antienne publiée dans le Compendium ; leur témoin doit être vérifié séparément.

collation.summary: French 2005 Compendium has mère du Verbe and imploré votre assistance / réclamé votre secours; the app instead says mère du Verbe incarné and réclamé votre intercession. FSSP publishes a closely related French traditional formula; it is a comparative devotional witness, not the original source edition of St Bernard.

uiNotice.en: This French Memorare follows a traditional variant independently attested by the FSSP; it differs from the 2005 French Compendium.
uiNotice.fr: Ce Souvenez-vous suit une variante traditionnelle également attestée par la FSSP ; il diffère du Compendium français de 2005.

collation.summary: The published Compendium has more than one English liturgical Magnificat version and a separate French text; edition and biblical translation must be displayed distinctly. No claim of complete 1962 Vulgate equivalence from this comparison alone.

uiNotice.en: The app's English Magnificat includes the appended office doxology, but French and Latin bodies finish at the biblical canticle. The 2005 Compendium publishes doxologies in its canticle forms; that is not an independently verified 1962 Breviary text. Keep the doxology context-dependent pending collation.
uiNotice.fr: Le Magnificat anglais de l’application ajoute la doxologie, alors que les textes français et latin s’arrêtent au cantique biblique. Le Compendium de 2005 publie des doxologies, sans établir pour autant le texte du Bréviaire de 1962. L’ajout liturgique reste à vérifier selon le contexte.

collation.summary: Compendium's English Anima Christi is a rhymed poem, whereas the app's English text is a direct prose translation of the Latin. The 2005 Latin text confirms the traditional original formula; French prose resembles the French appendix but all variants require complete comparison.

uiNotice.en: The English prose rendering is not the rhymed English text printed in the 2005 Compendium; the Latin original is provided for comparison.
uiNotice.fr: La version anglaise en prose diffère du poème anglais imprimé dans le Compendium de 2005 ; le latin permet la comparaison.

collation.summary: English Compendium prints alternative canticle renderings; French and Latin also have established liturgical texts. The app must declare which Bible/office wording it reproduces rather than treating all as one literal trilingual witness.

uiNotice.en: The app's English Benedictus includes a doxology, whereas French and Latin stop after the biblical verses. The French Compendium uses a distinct doxology referring to the God who is, was and is to come. Do not append an undifferentiated Gloria until the 1962 office and locale editions are collated.
uiNotice.fr: Le Benedictus anglais ajoute une doxologie, tandis que le français et le latin s’arrêtent au cantique biblique. Le Compendium français donne une doxologie particulière « au Dieu qui est, qui était et qui vient ». Ne pas la remplacer sans vérification du Bréviaire de 1962 et des éditions propres à chaque langue.
